Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers. Attached is our proposed Order Form (Aurora_OrderForm_v2.pdf). A few commercial notes from procurement that we wanted to confirm before we move this to legal:

- Net payment terms: 60 days after invoice (Aurora standard).
- Invoicing: they will send a single monthly invoice per entity; prefer EFT payments.
- Taxes: Aurora requires Redwood to accept our tax residency certificate and to confirm VAT handling (we expect Redwood to invoice without withholding, Aurora will self-report VAT where required).

Can you confirm a timeline for legal to review? We can provide a PO and tax certificate once we align on net terms and the invoicing entity.

Thanks for the ping — reviewed the draft at a high level and added an internal redline (Redline_Aurora_OrderForm_v3.pdf). High-level Legal notes:

1) Invoicing entity mismatch: the Order Form references 'Aurora Analytics, Inc.' but the PO from procurement may come from 'Aurora Analytics EU Ltd'. We should require the invoiced entity to match the billed entity clause and include a contact for invoice disputes.

2) Net terms: net-60 is outside our standard net-45 for named accounts. We can accept net-60 only if one of the following is included: (a) 10% upfront payment (applied to first invoice), (b) a credit application + finance sign-off, or (c) a rolling security deposit recalibrated quarterly. Recommend option (a) or (b) to keep commercial cadence simple.

3) VAT/Withholding: add explicit language that Redwood invoices without withholding; Aurora is responsible for VAT/resident taxes unless Redwood is required by law to withhold. Require receipt of government tax residency certificate before first invoice.

4) Minimum commit cadence: switching to quarterly tranches is acceptable but requires adjusting billing triggers and pro-rata logic in section 4 — Sales to confirm if pricing ladder tolerates smaller tranches.

5) Audit & evidence: add a 12-month audit clause limited to invoice verification, and require any tax certificates to be delivered to finance@redwood.ai.

I flagged these in the redline and marked change bars where countersign will be needed. If Sales wants to accept net-60 without upfront we need explicit Finance approval and a deal credit note to protect Redwood.

I'll attach the redline and a short comment summary. Happy to pair with you on the external response.

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redline_Aurora_OrderForm_v3.pdf, Redline_Summary.xlsx
